how.title: How the reading works
how.body: The reader extracts text from a PDF, DOCX or plain text file, rebuilding lines from glyph positions so line breaks and column gaps survive. Those signals tell it where one section ends and the next begins. The text is then scored across five dimensions worth 100 points: parseability 25, keyword match 25, structure 20, impact 20 and contact 10. Every lost point is charged to a named finding, with the line it came from and what to write instead, and findings are listed most expensive first. Without a job ad the keyword dimension is capped at 20 of 25 points, and the report says so. The reading and scoring run in your browser. To run an analysis you sign in, and the file, its text and the result are then stored on our server for 12 months.

upload.a: Yes. Your CV is read and scored in your browser first. When you analyze it, the file, its text and the result are also sent to our server and stored there. Details are in the privacy notice.

score.a: Five dimensions add up to 100 points: parseability 25, keyword match 25, structure 20, impact 20, contact 10. Every lost point is attached to a named finding with a fix.

languages.a: Section headings, action verbs and stopwords are recognised in English, German and Turkish, and the document language is detected automatically.

shared.q: What does a shared report store?
shared.a: Scores and advice only. The link carries no lines from your CV, and it expires after 30 days.

guarantee.q: Does a high score mean I will be invited?
guarantee.a: No. The checks are heuristics built from how mainstream parsers behave, not a reproduction of any named vendor. A good score means nothing stands between your CV and a human reader.

noAd.q: What changes without a job ad?
noAd.a: The keyword dimension is capped at 20 of 25 points and the report says so; a generic skill list is not a match score.

formats.a: PDF, DOCX and plain text files up to 10 MB. PDFs with a text layer work best; scanned images need OCR first.

retention.q: How long is my data kept?
retention.a: Twelve months from the upload date. After that, the file, extracted text and analysis result are deleted from the database and storage.

delete.q: How do I delete my data?
delete.a: Use the data request form to ask for erasure. We respond within 30 days. You can also contact us directly at the email in the privacy notice.

accuracy.a: The checks are built from how mainstream parsers behave. They are not a reproduction of any named vendor, but they catch the same issues a parser would: missing text layers, broken headings, tables that scramble contact details.

findings.columns: Multi-column layouts break the parser. Parsers read left to right, so two columns get mixed together. Use a single-column layout instead.
findings.encoding: Special characters (Turkish, German) appear broken. This happens when the PDF text layer uses the wrong encoding. Re-export the PDF with embedded fonts from the source document.
findings.quantify: Add numbers to your bullets. Instead of 'Responsible for sales', write 'Increased sales by 23% in Q3'. Numbers make your achievements concrete.
findings.verbs: Start each bullet with an action verb: built, migrated, automated, reduced. Avoid 'Responsible for' or 'Worked on' - they describe a role, not your contribution.
findings.contact: Add your email, phone and a LinkedIn or GitHub link near the top. These are the first fields a parser looks for.
findings.sections: Use standard section headings: Experience, Education, Skills. Parsers map these to fields. Unusual headings like 'My Journey' are not recognised.
findings.parseColumns: Columns can mix up reading order. Parsers read text in a linear order, so two-column layouts may interleave content. Use a single-column layout to keep the reading order intact.
findings.parseEncoding: Characters appear broken when the PDF encoding is wrong. This affects Turkish and German special characters. Re-export the PDF with embedded fonts from the source document.
findings.parseImageOnly: Text must be selectable. Image-only or scanned PDFs cannot be read by parsers. If your PDF is a scan, use OCR to add a text layer first.
findings.contactMissing: Contact fields are missing. Add email, phone and a profile link (LinkedIn or GitHub) near the top. These are the first fields a parser extracts.
findings.impactWeak: Impact is weak without numbers and action verbs. Start bullets with what you did (built, migrated, reduced) and add metrics where possible.
findings.keywordsMissing: Keywords from the job ad are missing. Add the required skills and technologies to your CV. The more terms that match, the higher the keyword score.

result.scoreDrop: Your score dropped because new findings were detected. Check the findings list - each one shows what changed and how to fix it. The most costly findings are at the top.
result.fixFirst: Start with the most costly findings at the top of the list. Each finding shows the points it costs and what to fix. Work down the list until the score improves.
result.whyScoreLow: Your score is {score} out of {totalMax}. You lost {totalLost} points. The main issues are: {topFindings}. Each costs {costs} points.
result.noJobAd: Add a job description to see which keywords are missing. Without an ad, the keyword dimension is capped at 20 of 25 points.
result.missingKeywords: You are missing {missing} from the job ad. You matched {matched} out of {total} keywords ({coverage}% coverage).
result.noStrengths: No standout strengths detected. Focus on fixing the findings to improve your score.
result.whatIsGood: Your CV has {count} strengths: {strengths}. Keep these as they are.

features.tailor: Tailor your CV to a job ad by pasting the ad text. The tool shows which keywords match and which are missing, so you can add the right terms.
features.compare: Compare multiple job ads side by side. See which keywords each ad requires and how well your CV matches each one.
features.interview: Prepare for interviews with story cards from your CV. The tool extracts achievements and maps them to common interview questions using the STAR method.
features.coverLetter: Generate a cover letter draft based on your CV and the job ad. The draft uses your actual achievements and matches the ad's requirements.
features.editor: Build a CV from scratch using the editor. Fill in your details, then export as PDF or DOCX. The editor follows ATS-friendly formatting.

facts.ats: ATS parsers extract text and fill profile fields like name, contact, job titles, employers, dates and schools. The exact behaviour differs by vendor and is not publicly documented in detail. The score here is a rule-based estimate of readability. It does not predict hiring outcomes.
facts.personalData: Photo, date of birth and marital status depend on country and employer. Some markets expect them, others do not. Check the market advice in your report for guidance.
